mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates aggressive monetary tightening amid persistent inflation, which typically triggers equity market sell-offs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions when HOUST declines by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown across manufacturing and housing sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines and HOUST declines by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In an inflationary regime (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%), the central bank's response of raising interest rates typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.
